answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a shale as the anchor of the cost.
